Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

response:
The legal criteria for 3rd party software include:

- **Data privacy and geo-location**: The geographic location of services and their data privacy agreements are carefully considered, especially for services provided by third-party service providers, as they may need to be listed in the Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) that virtualQ shares with its clients.

- **Regulatory compliance**: Due to handling data regulated by the EU’s GDPR, as well as customers governed by Sozialgesetzbuch (SGB) and critical infrastructure (KRITIS), requirements exceed standard security benchmarks like the BSI's C5 for secure cloud computing.

- **Access to data**: Even theoretical access to plain text data by third parties (e.g., managed service providers like AWS) is a concern. For example, Amazon RDS, while C5-compliant, cannot be used directly for SGB-regulated data because AWS could potentially access unencrypted data.

- **Encryption requirements**: Sensitive data stored in databases must be encrypted with customer-managed keys to prevent unauthorized access by third parties.

- **Licenses and IP ownership**: Open source components are evaluated for licensing compatibility, as not all open source licenses are suitable for integration into the virtualQ system.

- **Compliance proof**: The effectiveness of security measures must be provable, often through audits, penetration tests, or by using services already in scope for recognized compliance programs (e.g., C5, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27xxx).
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

response:
Internal and external audits are both processes used to evaluate and improve the security, architecture, and compliance of the virtualQ system, but they differ in scope, execution, and participants.

**Internal Audits & Design Verification** are conducted internally during the implementation phase to guide decision-making, particularly for strategic or architectural choices. These audits occur at regular decision points where different implementation options are evaluated. While minor decisions are handled within pull request reviews by engineers, larger architectural decisions are discussed and verified in dedicated internal meetings. A key component of internal audits is the use of the **AWS Well-Architected Framework**, which serves as a self-service audit tool for systems running on cloud or hybrid infrastructure. This audit evaluates six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimisation, and Sustainability. It identifies deviations from AWS best practices. The audit is conducted once or twice a year, with findings recorded as technical debt and prioritized based on criticality. Participants include the Head of Engineering, Lead Developer, and senior developers as needed.

**External Audits** involve third-party tools, services, or partners to verify the virtualQ system either in the codebase or in a non-production environment. These include automated verifications as well as manual security assessments such as **penetration testing**, which are carried out by an external partner. Additionally, external reviews are performed on a regular basis, and any findings are logged into a technical debt Jira project to ensure follow-up and resolution. These audits provide an independent validation of the system’s security and compliance posture.

The main differences lie in who conducts the audit (internal teams vs. external parties), the focus (architectural guidance vs. independent verification), and tools used (self-assessment frameworks like AWS Well-Architected vs. external tooling and manual penetration testing).
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

Bessere Benutzererfahrung (User Experience)Höhere Akzeptanz von BotsMöglichkeit zu Entscheiden den nächsten möglichen Termin zu nutzen (normales virtualQ) oder einen Termin zu buchen

response:
The legal criteria for 3rd party software include ensuring compliance with regulations such as GDPR, geo-location of services and their data privacy agreements, and evaluating licenses and IP ownership. Specifically, it is crucial to consider:

- Whether the data is encrypted at rest and in transit.
- Who has access to the data and if there is a business reason for it.
- The ability to prove the effectiveness of security measures.
- Any additional technical or organizational requirements from GDPR, Sozialgesetzbuch (SGB), or KRITIS that need to be taken into account.
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

Internal audits and design verification are carried out during the implementation phase. These include regular decision points where one feature implementation option must be selected over another. Smaller decisions are usually handled by engineers and verified in pull request reviews, while larger decisions or architectural guardrails are created in dedicated internal meetings or audits. Participants involved in these internal audits include the Head of Engineering, Lead Developer, and senior developers as needed.

External audits, on the other hand, are based on external tooling/services that verify the virtualQ system either in the codebase or in the live system at a non-production stage. Findings from these audits are tracked in a technical debt Jira project to ensure they are followed up on. These audits involve a partner for manual security-related audits like penetration testing. External audits are carried out on a regular basis.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots. 
Zusammenfassung: 
Bessere Benutzererfahrung (User Experience)Höhere Akzeptanz von BotsMöglichkeit zu Entscheiden den nächsten möglichen Termin zu nutzen (normales virtualQ) oder einen Termin zu buchen

**Legal criteria that must be evaluated before adopting any 3rd‑party software or service**

- **Compliance with data‑protection regulations**  
  - The software must respect the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).  
  - For customers subject to the German Social Code (SGB) or critical‑infrastructure (KRITIS) requirements, the solution must meet the stricter obligations defined by those regimes (e.g., BSI‑C5, PCI‑DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27xxx).

- **Geo‑location and data‑privacy agreements**  
  - The physical location of the service (or its data‑processing facilities) must be examined to ensure that data residency and cross‑border‑transfer rules are satisfied.  
  - All privacy‑related contracts (e.g., data‑processing agreements) have to be reviewed and, where necessary, listed in the DPAs that virtualQ shares with its clients.

- **Licensing and IP ownership**  
  - The software’s licence must be compatible with virtualQ’s need to integrate the component into its own system.  
  - For open‑source components, the licence terms (including attribution, copyleft, patent grants, etc.) must be understood and verified that they do not impose unwanted obligations.  
  - Ownership of any intellectual‑property rights that could affect future use or redistribution must be clear.

- **Avoidance of legal risk and lock‑in**  
  - The evaluation must confirm that adopting the software will not create legal exposure (e.g., infringement, breach of contractual terms).  
  - The solution should not lead to vendor lock‑in, end‑of‑life (EoL) problems, or other dead‑end scenarios that could jeopardise long‑term operability.

- **Proof of compliance and security effectiveness**  
  - It must be possible to demonstrate that the software’s security controls (encryption at rest/in‑transit, access controls, etc.) are effective and meet the applicable regulatory requirements.  

These criteria together ensure that any 3rd‑party library or service can be used without violating GDPR or other sector‑specific regulations, respects licensing obligations, and does not expose virtualQ to legal or operational lock‑in risks.

Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

response:
**Internal audits**

* **Who performs them** – Members of the product team (Head of Engineering, Lead Developer, senior developers and, when needed, other engineers).  
* **When they happen** – During implementation there are regular decision points; larger‑scale or architectural decisions are reviewed in dedicated internal meetings or audits.  
* **What they cover** – Design‑verification and compliance with internal guardrails.  The AWS Well‑Architected Framework is used as a self‑service audit for assets running on cloud or hybrid setups; it checks the six pillars (Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimisation, Sustainability).  
* **Outcome handling** – Findings are recorded as technical‑debt items in the internal Jira project and are followed up according to their criticality.  
* **Frequency** – Typically once or twice a year for the AWS audit; decision‑point reviews occur continuously throughout development.

**External audits**

* **Who performs them** – External parties: an external security advisor, a partner that conducts penetration testing, and external tooling/services. The executive sponsor (CEO) also participates.  
* **When they happen** – Carried out on a regular basis, independent of the internal development cycle.  
* **What they cover** – Verification of the virtualQ system (both code‑base and live, non‑production system) using external tools, plus manual security‑related audits such as penetration testing.  
* **Outcome handling** – Any findings are entered into the same technical‑debt Jira project so that they are tracked and remediated.  
* **Frequency** – Regular, but the exact cadence is not specified; it is driven by the external partner’s schedule and tooling cycles.

**Key differences**

| Aspect | Internal audits | External audits |
|--------|----------------|-----------------|
| **Performers** | Internal engineering leadership and developers | External security advisor, external partner, external tooling/services |
| **Scope** | Design verification, adherence to internal architectural guardrails, AWS Well‑Architected review | Independent validation of code and live system, penetration testing, compliance checks by third parties |
| **Trigger** | Built‑in decision points during implementation | Scheduled external reviews, tool‑driven checks |
| **Reporting** | Findings become technical debt tracked internally | Findings also become technical debt, but come from an outside source |
| **Participants** | Head of Engineering, Lead Developer, senior developers (and others as needed) | CEO, Head of Engineering, external security advisor, partner performing pen‑tests |
| **Frequency** | Typically once/twice a year for AWS audit; continuous for decision‑point reviews | Regular external reviews (frequency not detailed) |

In summary, internal audits are *in‑house* design and compliance checks driven by the development team, whereas external audits are *independent* evaluations performed by outside experts or tools, focusing on security and compliance from an outsider’s perspective. Both feed their findings into the same technical‑debt tracking system, but they differ in who conducts them, what they examine, and how they are initiated.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots. 
Zusammenfassung: 
Bessere Benutzererfahrung (User Experience)Höhere Akzeptanz von BotsMöglichkeit zu Entscheiden den nächsten möglichen Termin zu nutzen (normales virtualQ) oder einen Termin zu buchen

response:
The legal criteria for 3rd party software include:

- **Data privacy and geo-location**: The geographic location of services and their data privacy agreements are carefully considered, especially due to EU’s GDPR regulations. Services must align with data protection requirements, and third-party providers may need to be listed in Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) shared with clients.

- **Licenses and IP ownership**: Licenses are critically evaluated, particularly for open source components, as not all open source licenses are compatible with virtualQ’s legal and operational requirements.

- **Access to data**: Consideration is given to whether a third party (e.g., a managed service provider like AWS) could theoretically access plain text data. For regulated data (e.g., under GDPR, SGB, or KRITIS), this access may be unacceptable unless data is encrypted and controls are in place.

- **Compliance with regulatory standards**: Services must meet or exceed security and compliance requirements beyond standard frameworks like C5, especially for customers under GDPR, Sozialgesetzbuch (SGB), or critical infrastructure (KRITIS), which have stricter demands.

- **Provable security measures**: The effectiveness of security measures (e.g., encryption at rest and in transit) must be demonstrable, and additional technical or organizational requirements from relevant regulations must be addressed.
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

response:
The programming languages used in the virtualQ system are:

- **Ruby** (43% of the codebase)  
- **HTML / JavaScript** (24% of the codebase)  
- **Python** (11% of the codebase)  
- **.Net / C#** (9% of the codebase)  
- **Elixir** (7% of the codebase)  
- **Other** (6% of the codebase), which includes languages like Terraform Templates.

The codebase is being consolidated to:
- **Ruby and Elixir** for application logic,
- **HTML/JavaScript** for user interfaces,
- **Python** for machine learning and AI.

Note: .Net / C# is considered legacy (ACD connectors), no longer sold, and only maintained.

Internal and external audits are both processes used to evaluate and improve the security, architecture, and compliance of the virtualQ system, but they differ in scope, execution, and participants.

**Internal Audits & Design Verification** involve regular decision points during the implementation of features, where architectural or strategic decisions are evaluated. Smaller decisions are handled by engineers and verified through pull request reviews, while larger, strategic decisions or architectural guardrails are made in dedicated internal meetings. One key component of internal audits is the use of the **AWS Well Architected Framework**, a self-service audit tool provided by AWS. This audit assesses cloud or hybrid infrastructure across six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimisation, and Sustainability. It identifies deviations from best practices and is conducted once or twice a year. Findings are recorded as technical debt and followed up based on their criticality. Participants include the Head of Engineering, Lead Developer, and senior developers as needed.

**External Audits** are conducted using external tools or services to verify the virtualQ system, either in the codebase or in a non-production version of the live system. They also include manual security assessments such as **penetration testing**, carried out by an external partner. These audits focus on validating the system's security posture independently. Findings from external audits are also logged in the technical debt Jira project to ensure follow-up. External reviews occur on a regular basis.

The main differences are:
- **Internal audits** focus on architectural and strategic decision-making and are conducted using frameworks like AWS Well Architected, involving internal technical staff.
- **External audits** involve third-party tools and partners to independently verify system security and code integrity, emphasizing external validation and compliance.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

response:
The legal criteria for 3rd party software include:

1. **Data Privacy and GDPR Compliance**: We carefully consider the geo-location of services and their data privacy agreements, especially important for services run by 3rd party service providers. These services might need to be listed in the Data Protection Authorities (DPAs) that virtualQ shares with its clients.

2. **Licenses and IP Ownership**: Licenses are crucial when integrating open-source components into the virtualQ system, as not every open-source data comes with the highest requirements in the field of privacy. 

3. **Security Measures**:
   - The data should be encrypted at rest and in transit.
   - Determine who is able to access the data and ensure there is a legitimate business reason for it.
   - Prove the effectiveness of security measures.

4. **Additional Compliance Requirements**: 
   - Ensure compliance with GDPR, Sozialgesetzbuch (SGB), and KRITIS, which may have additional technical or organizational requirements beyond those defined by the Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der IT (BSI) for secure cloud computing (C5).

5. **Service Scope and Limitations**: Understand the service scope and limitations, such as Amazon Relational Database Service being in scope for C5 but not suitable for SGB customers due to AWS's ability to access plain text data in theory. Sensitive data stored in databases will be encrypted.
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

Internal audits and design verifications are carried out during implementation, focusing on regular decision points and larger (strategic) decisions. These are conducted in dedicated internal meetings or audits with participants like the Head of Engineering, Lead Developer, and senior developers as needed. The AWS Well Architected Framework is used for self-service audits focusing on six pillars (Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability), tracking findings as technical debt.

External audits are conducted on a regular basis to verify the virtualQ system either in the code base or the live system in a non-production stage using external tooling/services. These audits also include manual security-related audits (penetration testing) carried out by a partner. Findings from external audits are put into the technical debt Jira project to ensure they are followed up.

The key difference is that internal audits are part of the internal development process, focusing on strategic decisions and adherence to internal standards, while external audits are more about verifying the system against external benchmarking tools and security practices.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots. 
Zusammenfassung: 
Bessere Benutzererfahrung (User Experience)Höhere Akzeptanz von BotsMöglichkeit zu Entscheiden den nächsten möglichen Termin zu nutzen (normales virtualQ) oder einen Termin zu buchen

**Legal criteria that must be satisfied before adopting any 3rd‑party software or service**

- **GDPR compliance** – the software must respect the EU General Data Protection Regulation and any related data‑privacy obligations.  
- **Geo‑location & data‑privacy agreements** – the physical location of the service and the contractual data‑privacy terms are examined to ensure they meet the required privacy standards.  
- **Inclusion in virtualQ’s DPAs** – if the provider can potentially access virtualQ’s data, it must be listed in the Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) that virtualQ shares with its clients.  
- **Licensing & IP ownership** – all licences (including open‑source licences) and intellectual‑property rights are reviewed to confirm that they allow the intended integration and distribution of the component within the virtualQ system.  
- **Avoidance of lock‑in / EoL risk** – the chosen software must not create a dead‑end situation (e.g., vendor lock‑in, end‑of‑life without a migration path).  
- **Regulatory program scope** – for customers subject to additional regulations (e.g., SGB, KRITIS), the software must be usable within compliance programmes such as C5, PCI‑DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27xxx, etc., or be able to meet those requirements (e.g., through encryption, penetration testing).  

These criteria together ensure that the third‑party software can be used legally, safely, and without exposing virtualQ or its customers to regulatory or licensing violations.
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

response:
The virtualQ system is built with the following programming languages:

- **Ruby** – primary language for application logic (≈ 43 % of the codebase)  
- **Elixir** – also used for application logic (≈ 7 %)  
- **HTML / JavaScript** – used for the user‑interface layer (≈ 24 %)  
- **Python** – used for machine‑learning and AI components (≈ 11 %)  
- **.Net / C#** – legacy ACD connectors (≈ 9 %)  
- **Other languages** – e.g., Terraform templates and miscellaneous scripts (≈ 6 %)

The current consolidation focuses on Ruby and Elixir for core logic, HTML/JavaScript for the UI, and Python for ML/AI, while the legacy .Net/C# code remains maintained.

response:
**Internal audits**

* **Who carries them out** – Members of the product team: Head of Engineering, Lead Developer, senior developers (and, when needed, other engineers).  
* **When they happen** – During implementation there are regular decision points; larger (strategic) decisions or architectural guard‑rails are examined in dedicated internal meetings or audits.  
* **What they cover** – Design‑verification activities such as:
  * Selecting one implementation option over another.  
  * Checking that the solution follows the **AWS Well‑Architected Framework** (the self‑service audit that looks at the six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimisation, Sustainability).  
* **Frequency** – Typically performed **once or twice a year**.  
* **Outcome handling** – Findings are recorded as **technical debt** and tracked in the technical‑debt Jira project; they are followed up according to their criticality.

**External audits**

* **Who carries them out** – External parties: an external security advisor, a partner that performs penetration testing, and other third‑party tooling/services.  
* **When they happen** – On a **regular basis** (the schedule is not specified, but they are recurring).  
* **What they cover** – Verification of the **virtualQ system**:
  * Automated checks with external tooling/services on the code base or on the live system in a non‑production stage.  
  * Manual security‑related audits such as penetration testing.  
* **Outcome handling** – Any findings are entered into the same **technical‑debt Jira project** to ensure they are followed up.  
* **Participants in the review meetings** – Chief Executive Officer, Head of Engineering, and the external security advisor.

**Key differences**

| Aspect | Internal audits | External audits |
|--------|----------------|-----------------|
| **Conducted by** | Internal engineering team (Head of Engineering, Lead Developer, senior devs) | Independent third‑party entities (external security advisor, partner performing pen‑tests, external tooling/services) |
| **Focus** | Design verification, architectural guardrails, compliance with internal best‑practice frameworks (e.g., AWS Well‑Architected) | Security validation of the product (code‑base and non‑production environment) using external tools and manual penetration testing |
| **Trigger** | Regular decision points during implementation; scheduled self‑service audit (once‑twice a year) | Ongoing external review schedule; external tooling runs and partner‑led pen‑tests |
| **Outcome tracking** | Findings become technical debt, tracked internally | Findings also become technical debt, but originate from an external source |
| **Participants in audit meetings** | Primarily internal staff (engineering leadership) | Includes senior business leadership (CEO) and external security advisor |

In short, **internal audits** are performed by the organization’s own engineers to verify design choices and adherence to internal frameworks, while **external audits** are performed by independent third parties to independently validate security and compliance of the system. Both feed their findings into the same technical‑debt tracking system, but they differ in who conducts them, the tools/methods used, and the perspective they provide.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

response:
The legal criteria for third-party software include:

- **Data privacy and geo-location**: The geographic location of services and their data privacy agreements are carefully considered, especially due to EU’s GDPR regulations. Services must comply with strict data protection requirements.
  
- **Data access**: Special attention is given to whether a third party (e.g., a service provider like AWS) could theoretically access plain text data, which may disqualify certain managed services for use with sensitive data (e.g., from SGB or KRITIS customers).

- **Compliance requirements**: For customers regulated under GDPR, Sozialgesetzbuch (SGB), or critical infrastructure (KRITIS), compliance requirements exceed standard secure cloud computing standards like C5. Therefore, third-party services must meet these higher thresholds.

- **Licenses and IP ownership**: Open source components are evaluated for licensing compatibility, as not all open source licenses are suitable for integration into the virtualQ system.

- **Data encryption**: Sensitive data stored in third-party systems (e.g., databases) must be encrypted to prevent unauthorized access.

- **Documentation in DPAs**: Third-party service providers may need to be listed in Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) that virtualQ shares with its clients.
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

response:
Internal and external audits are both processes used to evaluate and improve the security, architecture, and compliance of the virtualQ system, but they differ in scope, execution, and participants.

**Internal Audits & Design Verification** refer to regular decision points during the implementation of features where architectural or strategic decisions are made. Smaller decisions are handled by engineers and verified through pull request reviews, while larger architectural choices or guardrails are established in dedicated internal meetings. One key component of internal audits is the use of the **AWS Well Architected Framework**, a self-service audit tool provided by AWS. This audit assesses cloud or hybrid infrastructure across six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimisation, and Sustainability. It identifies deviations from best practices and is conducted once or twice a year. Findings are recorded as technical debt and prioritized based on criticality. Participants typically include the Head of Engineering, Lead Developer, and senior developers as needed.

**External Audits**, on the other hand, involve reviews carried out by external parties using third-party tooling or services to verify the virtualQ system—either in the codebase or in a non-production environment. This includes manual security audits such as **penetration testing** conducted by a partner. These external reviews are performed regularly, and any findings are logged into the technical debt Jira project to ensure follow-up and resolution.

The main differences are:
- **Internal audits** focus on design decisions and architectural alignment with best practices (e.g., via AWS framework), and are led by internal staff.
- **External audits** involve independent verification of the system's security and code by outside tools or partners, providing an objective assessment of vulnerabilities.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots. 
Zusammenfassung: 
Bessere Benutzererfahrung (User Experience)Höhere Akzeptanz von BotsMöglichkeit zu Entscheiden den nächsten möglichen Termin zu nutzen (normales virtualQ) oder einen Termin zu buchen

response:
The legal criteria for 3rd party software include:

- **Geo-location of services and their data privacy agreements**: These are carefully considered, especially for services run by 3rd party service providers, as they might have to be listed in the Data Protection Authorities (DPAs) that virtualQ shares with its clients.

- **Licenses and IP ownership**: Licenses are crucial when integrating open source components into the virtualQ system. Not every open source data comes with the highest requirements in the field of privacy, so it is important to carefully consider any party that might (even in theory) be able to access our data.

- **Encryption**: For example, while Amazon Relational Database Service is in scope for secure cloud computing (C5), it cannot be used straight away in the context of SGB customers as AWS is (in theory) able to look at plain text data. Instead, any sensitive data that has to be stored in the database will be encrypted.

Additionally, we need to ensure that:
- The data is encrypted at rest and in transit.
- We can prove the effectiveness of our security measures.
- There are no additional technical or organizational requirements from GDPR, SGB, or KRITIS that we have to take into account.
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

response:
The central frameworks are:

1. **Ruby on Rails** - A model-view-controller framework written in Ruby. It simplifies and accelerates writing applications that exchange data with clients (via UIs or APIs), processes it, and stores the data in the database.

response:
**Internal Audits & Design Verification**

During implementation, there are regular decision points where one option for implementing a feature has to be selected over another. Smaller decisions are usually done by engineers and verified in the pull request review, while larger (strategic) decisions or architectural guardrails are created in dedicated internal meetings or audits. 

**External Audits**

External reviews are carried out on a regular basis. Any findings reported are put into the technical debt Jira project to ensure they are followed up on. External audits are based on external tooling/services verifying either the virtualQ system in the codebase or the live system in a non-production stage. Additionally, manual security-related audits (penetration testing) are carried out by a partner.

**Differences:**

- **Internal Audits**: These are conducted by the internal team, focusing on architectural guardrails, strategic decisions, and ensuring code quality through peer reviews in pull requests.
  
- **External Audits**: These involve external tooling/services and partners to verify the system, focusing on verifying the codebase or live system in a non-production stage and conducting penetration testing. Findings from external audits are tracked in the technical debt Jira project.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

**Legal criteria for using 3rd‑party software (as defined in the virtualQ documentation)**  

1. **Data‑protection & privacy compliance**  
   * The software must respect the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).  
   * Its hosting location and any cross‑border data transfers have to be evaluated (geo‑location of the service).  
   * The provider’s data‑privacy agreements must be reviewed and, if necessary, the service must be listed in the Data‑Processing Agreements (DPAs) that virtualQ shares with its clients.  

2. **Regulatory‑specific requirements**  
   * For customers subject to the German Social Code (SGB) or critical‑infrastructure (KRITIS) regulations, the service must meet the stricter controls defined by the Federal Office for IT Security (BSI) and the C5 secure‑cloud certification.  
   * If a service is not directly C5‑certified (e.g., a managed database like Amazon RDS), additional safeguards (e.g., encryption of data at rest and in transit, penetration testing) must be applied so that the overall solution inherits compliance with C5, PCI‑DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27xxx, etc.  

3. **Licensing & IP ownership**  
   * All licences of the 3rd‑party component must be examined.  
   * The licence must allow integration into the virtualQ system; not every open‑source licence is acceptable.  
   * Intellectual‑property ownership must be clear to avoid infringement or later legal disputes.  

4. **Access & control considerations**  
   * Identify who (the provider or any third party) can access the data and confirm that a legitimate business reason exists.  
   * Verify that the provider cannot read plain‑text data unless required and that encryption is enforced.  

5. **Proof of security effectiveness**  
   * The provider must be able to demonstrate that security measures are effective (e.g., through penetration tests, audit reports, or compliance certificates).  

6. **Avoidance of lock‑in and end‑of‑life risks**  
   * The selection process also checks that the software does not create a vendor lock‑in situation or expose virtualQ to a dead‑end if the product reaches end‑of‑life.  

**In short:** the legal criteria focus on GDPR‑aligned privacy handling, appropriate geo‑location, inclusion in DPAs, compliance with sector‑specific regulations (C5, PCI‑DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27xxx, etc.), clear licensing and IP rights, controlled data access, demonstrable security, and mitigation of lock‑in or EoL risks.
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

response:
**Internal Audits & Design Verification**

* **Who conducts them** – Carried out by the organisation’s own teams (Head of Engineering, Lead Developer, senior developers and, when needed, other engineers).  
* **When they happen** – During implementation, at regular decision‑points and at dedicated internal meetings/audits.  
* **What they cover** –  
  * Review of design and architectural choices (strategic/guard‑rail decisions).  
  * Use of the **AWS Well‑Architected Framework** self‑service audit, which checks the six pillars (Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimisation, Sustainability).  
  * Smaller decisions are verified in pull‑request reviews; larger strategic decisions are reviewed in the internal audit meetings.  
* **Outcome handling** – Findings are recorded as **technical debt** in the internal Jira project and are followed up according to their criticality.  

**External Audits**

* **Who conducts them** – Performed by external parties: an external security advisor, specialised partners, or third‑party tooling/services.  
* **When they happen** – On a regular basis (typically once or twice a year, but the cadence can vary).  
* **What they cover** –  
  * Verification of the **virtualQ** system using external tools/services, either against the code base or the live system in a non‑production environment.  
  * Manual security‑related audits such as **penetration testing** carried out by a partner.  
* **Outcome handling** – Any findings are entered into the same technical‑debt Jira project so that they are tracked and remediated.  

**Key Differences**

| Aspect | Internal Audits | External Audits |
|--------|----------------|-----------------|
| **Conducted by** | Internal staff (engineering leadership & developers) | External security advisors, partners, third‑party tools |
| **Focus** | Design verification, architectural guardrails, compliance with AWS Well‑Architected pillars; decision‑point reviews | Security validation of code and running systems, penetration testing, compliance checks from an outsider’s perspective |
| **Scope of tooling** | AWS Well‑Architected self‑service audit, pull‑request reviews | External tooling/services, dedicated penetration‑test engagements |
| **Frequency** | Regular decision points and internal meetings (often aligned with sprint/feature cycles) | Regular, typically annual or semi‑annual, but can be scheduled as needed |
| **Outcome tracking** | Findings become technical debt tracked internally | Findings also fed into the technical‑debt Jira project, but originate from an outside source |

In short, **internal audits** are **in‑house reviews** that verify design decisions and alignment with internal best‑practice frameworks, while **external audits** are **independent assessments** performed by third‑party experts or tools to validate security and compliance from an outside perspective. Both feed their results into the same technical‑debt tracking system, but they differ in who performs them, the tools used, and the primary focus of the review.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots. 
Zusammenfassung: 
Bessere Benutzererfahrung (User Experience)Höhere Akzeptanz von BotsMöglichkeit zu Entscheiden den nächsten möglichen Termin zu nutzen (normales virtualQ) oder einen Termin zu buchen

response:
The legal criteria for 3rd party software include:

- Ensuring compliance with data privacy regulations, particularly the EU’s GDPR, due to the regulated nature of the data handled.
- Carefully evaluating the geo-location of services and their data privacy agreements, especially for services provided by third-party providers, as they may need to be included in Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) with clients.
- Assessing licenses and intellectual property (IP) ownership, particularly when integrating open source components, as not all open source licenses meet the required legal standards.
- Considering additional regulatory requirements for specific customer types, such as those governed by the Sozialgesetzbuch (SGB) or critical infrastructure operators (KRITIS), which may impose stricter conditions than standard frameworks like BSI’s C5.
- Avoiding the use of managed services where the provider could theoretically access plain text data (e.g., Amazon RDS for SGB customers), unless sensitive data is encrypted appropriately.
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

response:
The central frameworks are:

1. **Ruby on Rails** - a model-view-controller framework written in Ruby that simplifies and accelerates writing applications that exchange data with clients (via UIs or APIs), process it, and store it in the database. The framework was first released in 2004 and has been widely adopted.

response:
Internal and external audits are both processes used to evaluate and improve the security, compliance, and technical quality of the virtualQ system, but they differ in scope, execution, and participants.

**Internal Audits & Design Verification** refer to reviews conducted within the organization during the implementation of features or architectural decisions. These audits focus on evaluating design choices, especially for larger or strategic decisions, and ensuring alignment with best practices. A key component is the use of the **AWS Well-Architected Framework**, a self-service audit tool provided by AWS, which assesses cloud or hybrid infrastructure across six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimisation, and Sustainability. The audit is performed once or twice a year, with findings recorded as technical debt and addressed based on criticality. Participants include the Head of Engineering, Lead Developer, and senior developers as needed.

**External Audits**, on the other hand, are carried out by external parties using third-party tools or services to verify the virtualQ system either in the codebase or in a non-production live environment. This includes manual security audits such as **penetration testing** conducted by a partner. These audits also occur regularly, and any findings are logged in the technical debt Jira project to ensure follow-up.

The main differences lie in who conducts the audit (internal teams vs. external partners), the focus (design and architecture vs. system-wide security and compliance), and the tools used (self-service frameworks like AWS vs. external tooling and manual testing). Both types contribute to identifying technical debt and ensuring continuous improvement in security and compliance.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots.

Bessere Benutzererfahrung (User Experience)Höhere Akzeptanz von BotsMöglichkeit zu Entscheiden den nächsten möglichen Termin zu nutzen (normales virtualQ) oder einen Termin zu buchen

The legal criteria for 3rd party software include:

1. **Geo-location of Services and Their Data Privacy Agreements**: 
   - Services and their data privacy agreements are carefully considered, especially for 3rd party service providers, which might have to be listed in the Data Protection Authorities (DPAs) that virtualQ shares with its clients.

2. **Licenses and IP Ownership**: 
   - Licenses, particularly for integrating open-source components, are evaluated to ensure compliance with legal standards.

3. **Regulatory Compliance**:
   - Compliance with regulations such as the EU’s GDPR, Sozialgesetzbuch (SGB), and requirements for critical infrastructure (KRITIS) is scrutinized. For instance, services like Amazon Relational Database Service, while in scope for certain secure cloud standards, may not be directly usable for SGB customers due to their managed service nature.
   
4. **Data Encryption and Access Controls**:
   - Sensitive data must be encrypted at rest and in transit. It’s important to determine who can access the data and ensure there is a legitimate business reason for such access.
   
5. **Security Measures and Tests**:
   - Security measures must be proven effective, e.g., through penetration tests, and compliance must be inherited by leveraging services that are in scope for relevant programs (e.g., C5, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27xxx).

6. **Technical or Organizational Requirements**:
   - Additional technical or organizational requirements from GDPR, SGB, or KRITIS must be taken into account.
expected_answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

The central frameworks for VirtualQ are:

- **Ruby on Rails**: A model-view-controller framework written in Ruby. response:
Internal audits and design verification are carried out during implementation and involve regular decision points where one option of implementing a feature has to be selected over another. Smaller decisions are usually done by engineers and verified in the pull request review, while larger (strategic) decisions or architectural guardrails are created in dedicated internal meetings or audits. Key participants include the Head of Engineering, Lead Developer, and senior developers as needed.

External audits are based on external tooling/services verifying the virtualQ system either in the codebase or the live system in a non-production stage. These audits focus on verifying findings reported by external tools and ensure they are tracked as technical debt in the Jira project. Further manual security-related audits (penetration testing) are carried out by a partner and are detailed in the "IT Infrastructure, Security & Compliance" section.

In summary, internal audits are more focused on the internal decision-making process and architectural guardrails, while external audits are focused on verifying findings from external tools and ensuring compliance and security.
expected_answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.

Demo
Beschreibung
Durch den Appointment2.0 Bot ist es möglich Termine direkt am Telefon zu buchen. Der Unterschied zum alten Termine per Voice ist, dass nicht mehr 3 Terminevom Bot vorgeschlagen werden und der Kunde diese durch drücken von Tasten bestätigen kann, sondern der Kunde kann selbst einen für ihn/ihr passendenTermin vorschlagen. Durch Speech Recognition (Spracherkennung) erkennt der Bot die “Eingabe“ des Kunden und kann darauf reagieren. Das drücken von Tastenist nicht mehr nötig. Alles passiert über Sprache. 
Ist der Appointment Bot aktiviert wird der Anrufer sofort zum Appointment Bot weitergeleitet. Dem Kunden wird dann vom Bot der frühstmögliche Termin angeboten(wie beim Queueing). Der Kunde kann diesen frühst möglichen Termin, dann per DTMF “1” akzeptieren oder mit “2” ablehnen und dann per Sprache einen anderenTermin buchen. Entschließt sich der Kunde einen anderen Termin zu buchen, dann nennt der Bot den Zeitraum in dem Termine zur Verfügung stehen (je nachdemwie es im Dashboard konfiguriert wurde), z.B. “Wir bieten Termine im Zeitraum von Montag bis Freitag den 26.04 von 10 bis 18 Uhr an“. Der Kunde kann nun seinenTermin buchen. 
Einrichtung
Um den Appointment Bot per Voice zu aktivieren muss die folgende Schritte ausgeführt werden: 
a) Termine für die Service Line im Dashboard aktivieren (nur als Admin möglich)b) Öffnungszeiten sowie Terminliche Rahmenbedingungen konfigurierenc) Einen Callflow auswählen, der “appointment” enthält.
Warum ein neuer Voice Bot? (Nutzen)
Der neue Bot bietet den Vorteil, dass der Kunde selbst entscheiden kann ob er/sie den nächstmöglichen Termin  (also wie ganz normales Queuing) oder einenspäteren Termin bucht. Für den Endkunden bietet das somit eine bessere User Experience. Eine bessere user Experience wird außerdem geschaffen in dem derKunde nicht mehr einer Liste von Terminen anhören muss um diese dann ggf. mit den Tasten zu bestätigen. Der Kunde kann ganz einfach und intuitiv durch Spracheeinen Termin buchen. Dies steigert außerdem die Akzeptanz von Bots. 
Zusammenfassung: 
Bessere Benutzererfahrung (User Experience)Höhere Akzeptanz von BotsMöglichkeit zu Entscheiden den nächsten möglichen Termin zu nutzen (normales virtualQ) oder einen Termin zu buchen
